summary_paragraph: A 30-year-old woman with Type 1 diabetes and a history of gastroparesis s/p gastric pacer presented with recurrent nausea and vomiting, just days after a prior discharge for similar symptoms. She had been tolerating oral intake until the morning of admission when she developed bilious, nonbloody vomiting. She was managed with NPO status, IV fluids, and IV antiemetics including ondansetron, prochlorperazine, and ativan. Her blood pressure, elevated on presentation, was controlled with IV metoprolol and transitioned back to oral lisinopril. Laboratory evaluation showed transient leukocytosis that resolved, mild hyponatremia (Na 130-132) likely due to vomiting and inappropriate ADH, and stable renal function. Blood and urine cultures showed no true infection. She gradually improved over 36 hours, advancing to a BRAT diet and oral medications. By discharge, she was tolerating oral intake, ambulating independently, and had stable vital signs. She was discharged home with continued antiemetics, insulin management guidance, and follow-up appointments with gastroenterology for pacer evaluation and her PCP for hypertension, hyponatremia, and cardiology referral.
problems: Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type I [juvenile type], not stated as uncontrolled
